title: Encoder agrees with $\sigma$ at variables fixed by $\rho_0$
statement: Fix $n$ and work with formulas on the variables $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$. Let $f$ be a DNF formula, $w \in \bbn$ a width parameter, and $\mathrm{fuel} \in \bbn$ a bound on the recursion depth; let $\mathrm{path}$ be a list of variable–value pairs (elements of $\mathrm{Fin}\,n \times \mathrm{Bool}$), let $\rho_0$ and $\sigma$ be restrictions on $n$ variables, and let $\mathrm{acc}$ be a list of index–value pairs holding the encoding accumulated so far. The recursive core of the Razborov encoder sends this data to a pair whose first component is again a restriction; write $\gamma$ for that restriction. Then for every variable $v$ that is fixed by $\rho_0$ — that is, $\rho_0(v) \neq \mathrm{none}$ — one has $\gamma(v) = \sigma(v)$.
hypotheses_covered: a DNF formula f on n variables
a path list of variable-value pairs
restrictions ρ₀ and σ on n variables
an accumulator list of index-value pairs
v is fixed by ρ₀ (ρ₀ v ≠ none)
caveat: The recursive helper razborovEncode.go is not defined in the provided snippet, so its computed meaning can only be gestured at as "the recursive core of the Razborov encoder"; the statement's shape (first component of the output pair equals σ at fixed variables) is fully rendered, but a graduate-quality description of what the encoder computes cannot be given faithfully from the material at hand.
